result.verdict: Not shippable as reviewed: the core approve/triage/control loops are visually calm and the state coverage is unusually thorough, but several P0 safety defects (sending while a draft is updating, acting on stale cross-space data, irreversible Send/Delete with no confirmation in view), systematic violations of your own glass/44pt/one-prominent-action rules in headers and composers, and below-the-fold burial of the founder's key destinations undermine the one-hand, between-meetings job.

findings.element: 'Send' button in draft card, 'Agent editing the draft' state (white pill, bottom-right of card) while header pill reads 'Updating' and 'Edit' is greyed out
findings.problem: Send remains fully enabled and is the sole white prominent action while the agent is mutating the draft. A one-handed founder can dispatch the pre-update text/recipient, or a half-updated body, with no indication the content is in flux.
findings.norm: Never allow submit during an in-flight mutation of the thing being submitted; disable and explain, or snapshot-and-label the sendable version.
findings.fix: Disable Send while 'Updating', replace the pill with 'Updating draft…', and re-enable only after the new draft is stable with a brief 'Draft updated' diff affordance.

findings.element: 'Send' button on 'Re: Pilot timeline / Needs approval' draft card (Thread) and red 'Delete chat' in Chat menu
findings.problem: Externally-visible email send and destructive delete are each one tap from these boards with no confirmation, undo, recipient address (only 'Ana Ruiz'), full original message, or consequence copy in view. For a founder approving between meetings this is an accidental-misfire and wrong-recipient risk.
findings.norm: Irreversible/external actions need either confirmation with specifics (to-address, subject, effect) or a robust undo window; destructive items need a confirm step.
findings.fix: Send opens a confirm sheet naming ana@… address, subject and 'This emails Ana Ruiz', or send with a 10s Undo toast; Delete chat requires a destructive confirmation sheet.

findings.element: 'Switching to Northwind' state: 'Northwind' title and fully populated PAGES rows ('Inbox 3 need reply', 'Finance 6 mo runway') under skeleton ACTIVITY/PERSONNEL placeholders
findings.problem: Pages show concrete, tappable numbers while the rest of the space is still loading — either stale Personal data under a Northwind title or unsynchronised partial data. The white '+ New' is also live. The founder can open or create in the wrong company.
findings.norm: A context switch must be atomic: content is either the old space (labelled) or fully the new space; no actionable cross-space residue during loading.
findings.fix: Skeletonise or dim-and-disable PAGES and '+ New' too, add 'Switching to Northwind…' status, and swap all sections together; block taps until loaded.

findings.element: Header glass groups in Thread: back chevron pill, 'Inbox agent' pill, right pill with Page/List/'...' icons, plus glass composer at bottom
findings.problem: That is four distinct floating glass groups (three in the header alone), breaching the brief's max-three-glass-groups-per-view rule, and the right pill crams three icon-only targets into one capsule so each is visibly narrower than 44pt.
findings.norm: Brief: glass only on floating nav/controls, ≤3 glass groups per view; Apple HIG 44×44pt minimum targets.
findings.fix: Merge back+agent into one header group (2 groups total with composer), move Page/List into the '...' Chat menu, and give any remaining icon a 44pt hit area.

findings.element: Top toolbar in Inbox: search/filter/compose capsule, '...' capsule, white chat bubble button (all states, e.g. 'Inbox', 'Archived, Undo')
findings.problem: Five icon-only actions, none labelled, three sharing one pill at sub-44pt width. A first-time founder cannot tell filter from compose from chat, and one-handed taps will mis-hit; the white chat button is also a second bright prominent element competing with page content actions.
findings.norm: Icon-only actions need familiar glyphs + accessible names + 44pt targets; one prominent tinted action per view (brief).
findings.fix: Keep Search as a labelled field/pull-down, put Filter and '...' in one menu, make Compose the single labelled prominent button, and demote chat to parity styling; widen hit areas to 44pt.

findings.element: 'Take control' / 'Release control' / 'Try again' / 'Retry' bottom bars and 'Team | Private' segmented control with 'X' (Watching)
findings.problem: Team↔Private is a bare segmented toggle with no confirmation or explanation although it changes who can see a shared machine — a privacy-critical mode switch placed casually next to Close. In 'In control' and 'Reconnecting' the X and Private segment disappear entirely, so the user cannot exit/close while driving or while reconnecting; only Release remains.
findings.norm: Privacy-scope changes need explicit consequence copy/confirmation; a modal/control state must always preserve an exit.
findings.fix: Tapping Private/Team shows a sheet ('Who can watch changes to…'); keep the X (44pt) visible in every state including In control/Reconnecting.

findings.element: Keyboard accessory row 'Esc Tab Ctrl ← ↓ ↑ →' in 'In control' and 'Agent waiting'
findings.problem: Seven grey-on-grey keys in a single pill overflow/clip at the right edge with no scroll affordance, each well under 44pt tall/wide — unusable one-handed for the exact task (driving a desktop) it exists for.
findings.norm: 44pt targets (brief/HIG), especially for precision control tasks; clipped content must signal scrollability.
findings.fix: Make keys ≥44pt, horizontally scrollable with edge fade, and keep only Esc/Tab/Ctrl/arrows; enlarge type contrast.

findings.element: Banner 'Sign in to the bank portal, then tap I'm done.' with 'I'm done' + text-only 'Skip' (Agent waiting)
findings.problem: A credential-entry handoff on a shared, watched computer carries no warning about who sees the screen, whether input is recorded, or what Skip does; 'Skip' is a small low-contrast text target beside the big white button. Highest-stakes moment in the app gets the least safety copy.
findings.norm: Credential/financial handoffs must state visibility/privacy and consequences; secondary actions need 44pt, legible targets.
findings.fix: Add 'Only you see typing while you drive; agents see the screen after I'm done' copy, make Skip a 44pt bordered button, and require Take control before any sign-in field is focused.

findings.element: 'Personal' Home (Connected): ACTIVITY + PERSONNEL + PAGES stacked; 'Data room' row cut off at the bottom edge, 'Team computer' not visible at all
findings.problem: The landing view does not fit one screen: Pages — a primary destination named in the brief — starts below the midpoint and is truncated mid-row with no scroll cue, so a first-time founder may never discover Data room/Team computer. Switching persona context, the equally key '+ New' competes with this scroll.
findings.norm: Primary destinations and the 'what needs me' summary must be legible within the first viewport on a 393×852 device; truncation needs a scroll affordance.
findings.fix: Compress Personnel to the 2–3 agents needing attention (or horizontal chips), keep ACTIVITY + a compact Pages grid above the fold, and add a bottom fade/scroll indicator.

findings.element: 'Needs you / Approve $1,200 payment' Finance agent row in ACTIVITY (Connected Home)
findings.problem: The single most urgent founder job — approving $1,200 — is just a chevron row with an amber 'Needs you' pill; there is no Approve/Deny affordance, amount is buried in 13pt subtext, so 'approve in a tap or two' becomes a navigation hunt.
findings.norm: Attention queues should expose the decision (approve/decline/details) inline or in one obvious tap, with the stakes (amount, payee) at headline hierarchy.
findings.fix: Make the row expand or route directly to an approval card with '$1,200 to [payee]' and Approve / Not now buttons ≥44pt.

findings.element: Right 'No model' Home: PAGES rows still show '3 need reply', '6 mo runway', '2 deadlines', 'Team computer • Online' under 'Connect a model to start chatting.'
findings.problem: Live-looking company data and badges persist in a state defined by 'no model', contradicting the premise and implying the inbox is actionable; tapping through presumably dead-ends. Left board has '+ New' and right board does not, with no explanation for the missing primary action.
findings.norm: Empty/unconfigured states must not present stale actionable data; primary actions should be consistent or explicitly disabled with reason.
findings.fix: Grey/skeletonise Pages badges until a model connects or add 'Connect a model' inline on each row; show '+ New' disabled with the same reason.

findings.element: 'Draft replaced' banner: 'Replaced by a newer draft' with clock icon, above the new draft card
findings.problem: The previous draft vanishes with an informational-only banner — no View previous, Undo, or diff. If the founder had reviewed/mentally approved v1, agent work silently overwrites it; trust-destroying for an approval workflow.
findings.norm: Agent overwrites of user-reviewable artefacts must be recoverable: keep version history/undo.
findings.fix: Add 'View previous' and 'Undo' (44pt) to the banner and a one-line diff ('10am → 10am, added invite line') on the new card.

findings.element: Plus menu (Photos / Files) floating card overlapping the draft's 'Edit' button in 'Plus menu' state
findings.problem: The attachment menu anchored to the composer's '+' renders mid-screen on top of the draft card, hiding Edit and visually associating Photos/Files with the email draft rather than the message being composed — wrong anchor, wrong context mid-approval.
findings.norm: Menus/popovers anchor to their invoking control; they must not occlude the primary task card.
findings.fix: Anchor the menu directly above the composer, dismiss the draft card highlight, or open the system photo/file picker as a sheet.

findings.element: 'Empty recipient' draft: 'Add a recipient' amber text and disabled grey 'Send'
findings.problem: 'Add a recipient' is a small text-only target under 44pt and reads as a status label, not a field; disabled Send gives no reason. The founder's fix path is the least tappable, least explained element on the card.
findings.norm: Blocking errors pair the disabled action with an actionable, ≥44pt fix field and plain-language reason.
findings.fix: Turn 'To' into a full-width tappable recipient field with placeholder 'Add a recipient', and caption Send: 'Add a recipient to send'.

findings.element: Legal agent block in Group thread: 'Legal agent' label, message bubble, then a second purple droplet avatar above the '•••' typing bubble
findings.problem: Two stacked purple avatars for one agent (message + typing) read as two different participants; combined with the overlapped orange/purple avatar cluster in the 'Funding room' header pill, a first-timer cannot tell how many bots are present or who is typing — and no name accompanies the typing indicator.
findings.norm: One avatar identity per participant per thread; typing indicators carry the participant's name.
findings.fix: Use a single avatar with the typing bubble inline, label it 'Legal agent is typing…', and separate header avatars with rings/count ('Finance, Legal').

findings.element: White round button with black square in Funding room composer (right of 'Message Funding room')
findings.problem: Per the 'Header and composer / Accessible names' spec this glyph means Stop, but in a chat composer a filled white circle is universally read as Send/record. While agents are typing the founder will tap it expecting to send and instead stop generation — the opposite outcome, unexplained.
findings.norm: Composer primary button must match the entered state: Send arrow when text exists, Stop only while generating and labelled as such.
findings.fix: Show a labelled Stop (square + 'Stop' tooltip/accessibility, distinct colour) only during generation; swap to an up-arrow Send once the field has text; empty state shows disabled send or mic.

findings.element: Inbox list rows: single-line truncation 'Re: Pilot timeline — Can we move the kickoff to Thu…' with right-aligned times and chips 'Draft ready/Needs attention/Junk/Newsletter'
findings.problem: Every sender reads identically at scanning distance; subject and snippet are concatenated and truncated, unread is a tiny white dot at the left edge (partly clipped in the swipe state), and chip taxonomy mixes state (Draft ready), urgency (Needs attention) and classification (Junk) in identical pills. Triage speed — the whole point of this screen — suffers.
findings.norm: Mail triage lists: bold sender, distinct subject line, 2-line snippet, consistent unread affordance, one chip semantics per dimension.
findings.fix: Two-line rows (sender/time, subject, snippet), reserve chips for state only, enlarge unread dot inside the row padding, and keep row height ≥60pt.

findings.element: Swipe-left reveal: 'Spam' and 'Archive' blocks behind 'Example Weekly' row, with content shifted off the left edge
findings.problem: Only left-swipe actions are shown, both are narrow (~56pt) grey blocks with low-contrast icon+label, Spam (a reporting/destructive-ish action) sits equal-weight beside Archive, and there's no full-swipe threshold hint, no right-swipe action (e.g. Reply/Done), and the partially hidden row text suggests the list is broken mid-gesture.
findings.norm: Swipe actions: colour-coded, ≥64pt, destructive/report actions separated or confirmed; support both directions with discoverability hints.
findings.fix: Colour Archive neutral/green, Spam amber/red with confirmation for senders, widen targets, animate a hint on first use, add right-swipe 'Needs reply/Done'.

findings.element: Consent screen 'Let the Inbox agent read your mail?' — 'Allow' white pill and 'Not now' plain text; header shows only a back chevron
findings.problem: The entire data-access decision rests on two vague lines ('It sorts mail and drafts replies. You approve anything it sends.'); no mail scope, retention, revoke path, or which account (me@example.test appears only in a different state). 'Not now' is a small grey text target. Consent this broad needs informed specifics, per App Store/privacy convention.
findings.norm: Permission priming must state scope, data use, and reversibility, with symmetric, ≥44pt choices.
findings.fix: List scope bullets (reads inbox, drafts only, revoke in Settings), show the account, and make 'Not now' a full bordered 44pt button.

findings.element: Space menu card (Personal / Northwind / Side project / New space + / Space settings) over Home
findings.problem: The menu is a solid dark card (not matching the glass treatment of other floating controls), truncates the 'Needs you' pill behind it ('eeds you'), the '+' and sliders icons right-align against left-aligned text rows creating a ragged tap map, and there's no dismiss X — a first-timer won't know tapping outside closes it. Rows for New space/Space settings are visually identical weight to switching spaces, mixing navigation with admin.
findings.norm: Menus anchor to their trigger with consistent control material, separated destructive/admin sections, and obvious dismissal; brief says floating controls are glass.
findings.fix: Use the same glass material as the header, add a divider and section label before New space/Settings, keep icons leading-aligned, and highlight the trigger 'Personal ⌄' as open.

findings.element: Status communication across boards: 'Working' blue dot, 'Done' green dot (Home ACTIVITY), 'Needs you' amber pill, 'Finance agent is driving' blue dot, 'Disconnected' red dot (Computer)
findings.problem: Meaning is carried by dot colour alone throughout, with three different encodings (dot+word in pills, dot+word inline, pill-only) for the same concept family. Colour-blind or bright-light one-hand glances lose Working vs Done vs Driving entirely.
findings.norm: Status must never rely on colour alone; pair with icon/text consistently (WCAG non-text contrast / Apple HIG).
findings.fix: Adopt one status component (icon + label, e.g. spinner/check/person) used identically on Home, Inbox chips and Computer, keeping colour as reinforcement only.

findings.element: Whole boards (all six files): each screen shows one phone per state on a shared 393×852 grid, with content areas largely empty black in Thread/GroupThread (top two-thirds blank) while Inbox/Computer fill to the home indicator
findings.problem: Chat states anchor a single exchange to the bottom leaving a vast empty void with no history, date divider, agent intro or context — first-time users land in an apparently empty room and cannot tell if history failed to load; conversely Inbox rows run flush to the home-indicator with no bottom inset. Density discipline is inconsistent across the journey.
findings.norm: Chat opens anchored to recent context with history/intro; lists respect safe-area bottom padding; empty space should carry orientation (who this agent is, what it can do).
findings.fix: Add an agent header card ('Inbox agent — searched mail, 12 results' as a proper message), seed history above the fold, and add 16pt bottom safe padding to Inbox/Computer content.

excellent: PH-Thread.png — the draft-approval card itself is exemplary: subject, 'Needs approval' pill, recipient, body and a single white 'Send' paired with subordinate 'Edit' makes the founder's decision legible in one glance.

PH-Inbox.png — state coverage is outstanding for a design board: Archived+Undo, 'Couldn't archive / Try again', Inbox zero with sync time, Gmail reconnect, mail-changes-off, no-account, consent and first-sync skeleton are all explicitly designed rather than hand-waved.

PH-Computer.png — the Watching→In control→Agent waiting→Control ended/Reconnecting/Control denied/Can't connect sequence honestly models a shared-machine lifecycle, and persistent plain-language status pills ('Finance agent is driving', 'You are driving') are exactly right for glanceability.
PH-Home.png — Connected vs No model side-by-side, with 'Connect a model to start chatting' and a single prominent 'Connect a model' action, makes the unconfigured state immediately understandable.

PH-Thread.png — including an 'Accessible names' spec panel mapping glyphs (Plus=Attach, Mic=Dictate, Round square=Stop, Pill with dot='Needs approval, go to draft') shows accessibility intent rarely present at this stage.
PH-GroupThread.png — naming each bot above its bubble ('Finance agent', 'Legal agent') with distinct avatars, plus a visible typing indicator, sets up multi-agent attribution correctly in principle.

result.verdict: Praci shows strong product thinking, disciplined dark-mode visual restraint, and thorough edge-case state planning, but several critical interaction traps (an enabled Send button while an AI agent is actively rewriting a draft, missing exit controls during remote computer sessions, and top-of-screen Undo toasts out of one-handed thumb reach) plus violations of the brief's own Liquid Glass group count and 44pt touch-target rules must be resolved before implementation.

findings.element: Draft card 'Send' button in 'Agent editing the draft' state
findings.problem: While the status badge on the draft card reads 'Updating' and the 'Edit' button is disabled, the prominent white 'Send' button remains fully enabled and highlighted as the primary action.
findings.norm: Destructive or irreversible commit actions (like sending an email) must be disabled or replaced by a stop/wait state while an asynchronous AI rewrite is actively mutating the payload.
findings.fix: Disable and dim the 'Send' button (matching the disabled 'Edit' button treatment) whenever the draft card is in the 'Updating' state, and add a subtle inline spinner inside the 'Updating' badge.

findings.element: Top-left navigation pill in 'In control', 'Agent waiting', and 'Reconnecting' states
findings.problem: When transitioning from 'Watching' to 'In control', 'Agent waiting', or 'Reconnecting', the close ('X') button disappears completely, leaving only a non-dismissible 'Team' badge in the top-left corner.
findings.norm: Users must always have an obvious escape hatch to exit a view, especially during degraded network states like 'Reconnecting' where 'Release control' may not respond.
findings.fix: Keep a dedicated 44pt circular 'X' (Close) button visible in the top-left corner across all eight computer states so the founder is never trapped on the remote desktop screen.

findings.element: 'Personal' vs 'Northwind' space content and 'PAGES' section during space switching
findings.problem: In PH-Home.png, the 'Personal' space displays B2B company agents and pages ('Carta agent', 'Mercury agent', 'Cap table', 'Data room', '6 mo runway'). Then in PH-Spaces.png ('Switching to Northwind'), 'ACTIVITY' and 'PERSONNEL' show loading skeletons while 'PAGES' continues displaying the exact same live metrics ('3 need reply', '6 mo runway', '2 deadlines', 'Online') without a loading state, and '+ New' remains active.
findings.norm: Switching workspaces must clear or skeletonize all workspace-scoped sections simultaneously so stale data from the previous space cannot be mistaken for the target space's data.
findings.fix: Show skeleton placeholders for the 'PAGES' card alongside 'ACTIVITY' and 'PERSONNEL' while switching to Northwind, disable '+ New' until the space finishes loading, and use personal-appropriate sample content in the 'Personal' space on PH-Home.png.

findings.element: 'PERSONNEL' list timestamps and preview copy in 'Connected' state
findings.problem: The 'PERSONNEL' list is out of chronological order ('2:59 PM', then 'Yesterday', then '2:44 PM', then '2:06 PM'), and the 'Inbox agent' row has a direct copy contradiction: its subtitle reads 'Sorted 14 emails this morning' while its timestamp reads 'Yesterday'.
findings.norm: Activity and chat lists sorted by recency must follow strict reverse-chronological order, and relative timestamps must agree with the preview copy.
findings.fix: Update 'Inbox agent' timestamp to a morning time (e.g., '9:15 AM') and order the 'PERSONNEL' rows consistently by most recent activity ('2:59 PM', '2:44 PM', '2:06 PM', '9:15 AM').

findings.element: Floating 'Archived / Undo' and 'Couldn't archive / Try again' toast banners
findings.problem: After swiping to archive an email, the floating 'Undo' and 'Try again' banners appear at the very top of the screen, obscuring the 'Inbox' title and requiring a full-screen stretch to the top-right corner.
findings.norm: For a one-handed mobile user (explicitly specified in the brief's persona), time-sensitive 'Undo' snackbars belong at the bottom of the viewport within natural thumb reach and should not cover page titles.
findings.fix: Anchor the 'Archived / Undo' and 'Couldn't archive / Try again' floating banners above the bottom home indicator within the one-handed thumb zone.

findings.element: Floating glass control groups and multi-icon pills across Inbox, Thread, GroupThread, and Computer views
findings.problem: Multiple screens violate the brief's explicit rules ('at most three glass groups per view' and 'touch targets 44 pt'): (1) PH-Inbox.png has 4 top-bar pills plus a 5th toast pill, and its 3-icon '[Search | Filter | Compose]' pill squeezes each icon into ~35pt width; (2) PH-Thread.png and PH-GroupThread.png use 4 glass groups (3 in the header + 1 composer) and squeeze 3 header icons ('[Page | List | More]') into ~35pt widths; (3) PH-Computer.png ('In control' and 'Agent waiting') stacks 4–5 floating groups and squeezes 8 keyboard keys ('⌨️', 'Esc', 'Tab', 'Ctrl', '←', '↓', '↑', '→') into ~36x32pt targets.
findings.norm: iOS Human Interface Guidelines and the brief require a minimum 44x44pt hit target for every interactive control and a maximum of three floating glass groups per view.
findings.fix: Consolidate top-right utility icons so each button has at least a 44x44pt frame, remove the glass pill around non-interactive thread titles ('Inbox agent', 'Funding room') to stay within 3 glass groups, and make the remote computer key bar horizontally scrollable with 44pt-tall keys.

findings.element: Top-left '[ X | Team | Private ]' control group in PH-Computer.png
findings.problem: The close ('X') button is fused inside the same glass capsule as the 'Team / Private' segmented picker, and the active 'Team' segment uses a bright solid-white pill fill identical to the bottom primary CTA ('Take control'). This violates the 'one tinted prominent action per view' rule and risks accidental screen dismissal when tapping 'Team'.
findings.norm: Navigation dismissal ('X') must be separated from mode/scope segmented controls, and segmented selection states should not compete visually with the screen's primary CTA.
findings.fix: Separate 'X' into its own 44pt circle button, move the 'Team | Private' switcher into a distinct pill with a subtle elevated glass selection fill rather than solid white, and reserve solid white exclusively for the bottom CTA.

findings.element: 'Mail changes off' and 'Gmail needs reconnecting' warning cards
findings.problem: In 'Mail changes off' and 'Gmail needs reconnecting', the top-right chat icon retains the solid-white prominent button treatment, forcing the urgent recovery actions ('Turn on' and 'Reconnect') into low-contrast dark grey pills. Additionally, 'Mail changes off' contains leaked developer placeholder text ('me@example.test').
findings.norm: When a system disconnection blocks core page functionality, the recovery CTA ('Reconnect') should hold visual priority, and placeholder strings must be replaced with realistic persona data.
findings.fix: Promote 'Reconnect' and 'Turn on' to higher-contrast prominent actions (demoting the top-right chat icon to standard glass when in an error state) and replace 'me@example.test' with a realistic founder address such as 'alex@northwind.ai'.

findings.element: Popover menus in 'Plus menu', 'Message menu (long press)', and 'Chat menu'
findings.problem: Menu presentation is inconsistent across thread states: in 'Plus menu', the attachment menu overlaps the draft card and clips the 'Edit' button without dimming the background; in 'Chat menu' (PH-Thread.png), the background and bright white 'Send' button remain undimmed (whereas 'Chat menu' in PH-GroupThread.png does dim the background); and in 'Message menu (long press)', all other messages in the thread vanish completely while the selected bubble shifts toward the center and re-wraps its text.
findings.norm: Context menus and popovers should apply a consistent backdrop dim across screens, preserve the spatial position and line wrapping of the long-pressed message, and keep surrounding context visible (dimmed/blurred rather than deleted).
findings.fix: Apply a consistent subtle backdrop dim when opening 'Plus menu' and 'Chat menu', and in 'Message menu (long press)' keep the rest of the thread visible under a dimmed blur while anchoring the highlighted user bubble in its original right-aligned position.

findings.element: 'Draft replaced' row and 'Header and composer' accessible names spec
findings.problem: In 'Draft replaced', the collapsed 'Replaced by a newer draft' box appears above 'Inbox agent searched mail, 12 results' immediately after a single user prompt with no intervening revision request, making it unclear why a draft was created and replaced before mail was even searched. Also, the 'Header and composer' table documents a 'Pill with dot' ('Needs approval, go to draft') element that is not shown on any screen.
findings.norm: Conversational audit trails must follow causal chronological order, and documented accessibility components should correspond to visible UI states.
findings.fix: Place the first tool call before the replaced draft (or include the user follow-up message that triggered the replacement), and either illustrate the floating 'Needs approval, go to draft' pill state on the board or remove it from the spec table.

findings.element: 'Legal agent' typing indicator and avatar in 'Group thread'
findings.problem: Directly beneath 'Legal agent's message (which already displays the purple teardrop avatar at its bottom-left), the active typing indicator repeats the exact same purple teardrop avatar a second time, and wraps a circular progress arc around the bottom-left of the non-circular teardrop shape, creating uneven radial spacing.
findings.norm: Consecutive bubbles from the same sender should not repeat the sender's avatar on adjacent rows, and circular progress rings should wrap circular containers.
findings.fix: Either merge the typing/working indicator into the Legal agent's message group without duplicating the avatar, or place the agent icon inside a circular badge so the progress ring is concentric.

findings.element: Email list states in 'Swipe left: Archive, Spam' and 'First sync'
findings.problem: Comparing 'Inbox' (cell 1) with 'Swipe left: Archive, Spam' (cell 2), the 'To do' card at the top of the Inbox disappears without explanation. On the swiped row ('Example Weekly'), the 3-line row collapses into 2 lines with '3:02 PM' floating above the middle of the snippet, and both 'Spam' and 'Archive' swipe actions share the same neutral grey fill. Additionally, in 'First sync' (cell 10), top-right 'Search', 'Filter', and 'Compose' buttons remain active while the inbox is still syncing its very first load.
findings.norm: Swiping a row must preserve the page layout and row typography while differentiating destructive/spam actions from archive, and search/filter controls should be hidden or disabled during initial sync.
findings.fix: Keep the 'To do' section consistent across active inbox states, preserve the 3-line email row layout when translated left, give 'Spam' a distinct semantic tint (e.g., muted red/orange), and hide or disable search/filter pills during 'First sync'.

findings.element: Status badge in 'Agent waiting' state
findings.problem: In 'Agent waiting', the bottom keyboard bar ('Esc', 'Tab', 'Ctrl', arrows) is active and the banner instructs the user to 'Sign in to the bank portal, then tap I'm done', which means remote input control has been handed to the user. However, the status pill only says 'Finance agent is waiting for you' (amber dot) rather than confirming that the user's keyboard/touch input is currently live on the shared computer.
findings.norm: When a remote desktop session activates local input capture, the status indicator must clearly communicate that the user is currently driving/controlling the screen.
findings.fix: Update the status badge or banner copy to make control state explicit (e.g., 'Your turn · You are driving') so the founder knows they can immediately tap and type into the bank portal.

findings.element: 'ACTIVITY' header 'See all' button and 'PERSONNEL' section surface
findings.problem: In 'Connected', 'ACTIVITY' and 'PAGES' are enclosed in rounded card containers with row dividers, whereas 'PERSONNEL' rows sit directly on the background canvas without a card surface or dividers. Additionally, the 'See all' action on the 'ACTIVITY' header is rendered in small muted text cramped against the top-right corner of the card, well under a 44pt vertical touch target.
findings.norm: Peer list sections on the same dashboard should share consistent container and divider grammar, and section header actions must provide adequate hit padding.
findings.fix: Place 'PERSONNEL' inside a matching rounded card container with row dividers (or add trailing chevrons to match interactive rows) and increase the tap target padding and legibility of 'See all'.

findings.element: Space switcher dropdown menu in 'Space menu (Personal still shown)'
findings.problem: In the open space menu, 'New space' and 'Space settings' below the divider are indented on the left by the width of the selection checkmark column while their own '+' and settings icons are placed on the far right, leaving an awkward blank gutter on the left.
findings.norm: In iOS pull-down menus, action rows with trailing icons either align flush-left when grouped in a separate section or place all icons consistently in the leading column.
findings.fix: Align 'New space' and 'Space settings' labels closer to the left margin of their section (or move the '+' and settings icons into the leading column) and dim the background content while the space menu is open.

excellent: Comprehensive state coverage across every journey step—including rare but crucial states like 'Draft replaced', 'Empty recipient', 'Archive failed, row stays', 'Mail changes off', 'Control ended', 'Control denied', and 'Reconnecting'.
Crisp, jargon-free microcopy tailored to a busy founder ('3 need reply', '6 mo runway', 'Needs you', 'Your keys are paused until it is back') that surfaces status and next actions immediately.
High-contrast dark visual hierarchy where the single solid-white primary action ('+ New', 'Send', 'Take control', 'Allow', 'Connect a model') stands out effortlessly against dark elevated surfaces.
Streamlined inline email approval card in PH-Thread.png that displays recipient, subject, and body directly inside the conversation for one-tap 'Send' sign-off.
